issue_context.title: [QUIC] Update to msquic 2.0
issue_context.body:
Once MsQuic 2.0 is released: https://github.com/microsoft/msquic/pull/2254, we should update to it.
Note that there are breaking changes in 2.0.
Also we'll need to update published packages to consume in tests/stress on Linux (I'm not sure, whether we build it from source or download from packages.microsoft.com atm).

Also we'll need to update published packages to consume in tests/stress on Linux (I'm not sure, whether we build it from source or download from packages.microsoft.com atm).
Author: ManickaP
Assignees: -
Labels: `area-System.Net.Quic`
Milestone: 7.0.0
It may be good time to switch to their packaging... (if ready)

To .NET , 2 of the breaking changes will matter.

Remove Level from SetParam/GetParam (#2322) 
This is a trivial fix, its just removing a prameter.

Add support for async listener stop (#2346)
This was something asked by the .NET team, and should theoretically be easy to support.

We do plan on having soversion support in 2. I'm not sure our packaging will be ready to go however.
Looks like we're unblocked and can start updating to 2.0 https://github.com/microsoft/msquic/discussions/2437

review_comments: Is it intentional that it will be "success" even before the event arrives?

Yes, we check it only in shutdown complete to unblock pending operations with proper exception. There's no point in distinguishing between start not called yet and  called and succeeded.
I also assume this will get reworked with #67302.
Is this change intended?

Yes, `Conditional` makes the test ignore the `SkipException`, otherwise it fails.
I assume the tests in CI might run without IPv6 support (only docker) so it didn't cause noise on your PR, but it was on my machine.
I was wondering why `SkipException` sometimes fails and other times skips...., thanks.
Since the stream start is asynchronous now, do we need to do anything to prevent stream operations before we get the StartComplete callback?
Most possibly, but I believe it will be part of https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/67302 (I also mentioned it in additional thoughts there)

msquic can handle stream operation before the stream is started, so we don't have to prevent anything. But tests and behavior depending on max stream limit is broken now. #67302 should be of very high priority now thanks to this.

> behavior depending on max stream limit is broken now

only throwing on reaching the limit is broken, right? the wait loop implemented in H3 should be fine? @ManickaP
That's my understanding.

FYI, it might be worth having a conversation about the `FAIL_BLOCKED` usage here. MsQuic allows you to start a stream and send on it before starting a connection (practically a requirement for 0-RTT scenarios), and without this flag it allows you to queue safely. But with this flag, it would just fail because you are blocked on starting the connection. It _might_ make sense to use this in your HTTP/3 scenarios, but not universally.
Yes, we do plan to rework stream starting in #67302. We have more issues around this than just 0-RTT :smile:
We need to wait for stream start callback event in all cases.

We should look into using MsQuic's [generated interop](https://github.com/microsoft/msquic/blob/main/src/cs/lib/msquic_generated.cs) layer instead of doing all this manually in .NET. Several of these enums are out of date, and don't include all the latest values.
Yes, at first we've planned to do both of the changes together, but later decided to split to a separate issue https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/67377
Sounds good!
We added this async stop functionality at the request of .NET. 😄 We were told it would make things easier for you!
Yes, I have it in my TODO list and plan to address. This is just a hack to get it working and be able to move forward, I'm aware it's ugly as heck :smiley:
We still get SHUTDOWN_COMPLETE if the connection start fails. If we free the context object here, the callback gets random memory and blows up.
Can we please leave this as a comment in the code?

I don't think it makes sense now since we only free the GC handle in failed ctors and in SHUTDOWN_COMPLETE, which makes sense.
Before this change, the call to free in failed connect was rather out-of-place.
